stories.title: Democrats notch early midterm wins as control of Congress remains unresolved
stories.summary: The Associated Press has called several early Democratic wins: Roy Cooper flipped North Carolina's Republican-held Senate seat, Jon Ossoff retained Georgia, Chris Pappas won New Hampshire, and Democrats flipped a Republican-held House seat in North Carolina. AP's live results say Democrats need three additional net Senate gains for a majority. Control of either chamber remains unresolved as more races are counted; AP race calls are projections, not final state certifications.
stories.why: A change in either chamber would reshape the final two years of the Trump administration, affecting legislation, budgets, nominations and congressional oversight.

stories.title: Russian strikes kill at least 31 at Ukraine aid site and hit energy infrastructure
stories.summary: The Associated Press reports at least 31 people were killed when a former school used as a humanitarian aid distribution site in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, was struck; more than 45 people remained missing. In a separate overnight barrage, Ukraine said Russia launched 289 drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions. Ukraine's DTEK said three thermal power plants halted operations. Moscow said it targeted military units and energy facilities; details of the aid-site attack are reported primarily through Ukrainian officials.
stories.why: The attacks deepen the civilian toll and threaten electricity and heating as winter approaches. They also cast doubt on prospects for the US-brokered Russia-Ukraine talks scheduled for November 10–11 in Abu Dhabi.

stories.title: Binance details $6.3 billion hack that began with a fake job interview
stories.summary: Binance says the October 29 theft from its internet-connected wallets followed a months-long intrusion: a tampered developer tool was downloaded in June, then a second engineer was lured into installing malicious code during a fake recruitment process in September. Attackers later used compromised computers, stolen credentials and an internal AI tool to reach wallet systems. Binance says about $2.85 billion in assets were frozen or intercepted. The FBI attributes the operation to a North Korean hacking group; Pyongyang denies involvement.
stories.why: The incident shows how social engineering, compromised developer tooling and access to internal systems can combine into a catastrophic breach. Engineering teams should verify software sources, isolate development environments and tightly control wallet-signing credentials.

stories.title: Vietnam's 10-month trade turnover tops $1 trillion for the first time
stories.summary: Vietnam's goods trade reached $1,010.55 billion in January–October 2026, up 32.3% year over year, according to figures from the National Statistics Office reported by VOV. Exports totalled $499.24 billion, up 27.5%, while imports reached $511.31 billion, up 37.4%, leaving a $12.07 billion trade deficit compared with a $19.49 billion surplus in the same period last year. October alone recorded a $7.31 billion surplus.
stories.why: The milestone underlines Vietnam's growing role in global manufacturing and supply chains. But faster import growth and the shift to a cumulative trade deficit highlight the importance of import costs, production inputs and the contribution of domestic firms versus foreign-invested exporters.

stories.title: Bull and Schwarz Digits plan a Europe-controlled AI and cloud stack
stories.summary: French computing company Bull and Germany's Schwarz Digits signed a memorandum of understanding to develop AI and cloud infrastructure operating under European jurisdiction. Schwarz Digits would provide its STACKIT cloud platform, while Bull would manufacture AI and high-performance-computing servers in Europe. The plan includes bringing Bull's AI platform to STACKIT and co-designing servers around Open Compute Project standards, with possible future SAP and quantum-computing work. This is a preliminary agreement, not an operational service; financial terms were not disclosed.
stories.why: The partnership is part of Europe's effort to build AI capacity for businesses and public institutions without placing sensitive infrastructure and data outside European legal control. Its impact will depend on actual deployment, price, compute capacity and software support.
